title: SLO-aware progressive circuit breaker with feature-degrade flow and on-call scriptlet library
content:
description:
Build a production-ready SLO-aware progressive circuit-breaker that can (1) auto-escalate degradation modes by region, (2) trigger a lightweight feature-degrade path (graceful feature flagging) to shed non-critical work, and (3) surface operator-facing scriptlets for on-call to safely run containment and recovery steps. The feature aims to reduce noisy paging by resolving transient overloads automatically and providing clear, low-effort operator actions when manual intervention is required.

acceptance_criteria:
Circuit-breaker exposes a per-route SLO heat metric and transitions through states: CLOSED -> SLIGHT_DEGRADE -> AGGRESSIVE_DEGRADE -> OPEN
Automated degrade actions are implemented as a pluggable feature-degrade adapter that can disable or soften non-critical subfeatures without dropping core traffic
Pager noise reduction measured: at least 40% reduction in minor P1 pages for load-induced SLO misses during synthetic traffic tests
On-call scriptlet library deployed to the runbook repo with atomic commands and safety checks; documented and linked from incident pages
Fallback and rollback paths are tested end-to-end in canary region and multi-region failover scenario
Metrics and dashboards (per-region SLO heatmap, degrade-state timeline, rate of degraded requests) are present in Console and alert thresholds updated

tasks:
Design circuit-breaker state machine and SLO heat scoring algorithm
Implement feature-degrade adapter interface and two sample adapters (tokenize-cache-policy, nonessential-metrics-scraper)
Integrate circuit-breaker state changes with routing layer to enforce degraded responses
Create operator scriptlet library and publish to runbooks repo
Add telemetry queries and dashboards to Console
Write automated integration tests that simulate regional capacity loss and validate degrade/rollback behavior
Ship a canary rollout in us-west-2 then gradually expand to eu-west-1

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 - Canary (us-west-2): enable SLIGHT_DEGRADE only, monitor 72h
Phase 2 - Limited expansion (us-west-2 + eu-west-1): enable SLIGHT + AGGRESSIVE_DEGRADE for low-traffic routes, run synthetic chaos tests
Phase 3 - Full rollout: expose feature to dedicated customers behind feature flag, ensure runbook snippets present in Console incident card
Rollback: feature flags per-region and per-customer; immediate rollback path documented in runbook_snippets

runbook_snippets:
scriptlet: rollback-degrade.sh - verifies circuit state, disables feature-degrade adapters, and re-evaluates SLO heat (safety: require operator confirmation)
scriptlet: quick-bridge.sh - creates a temporary routing rule to route 10% traffic to fallback model variant during multi-region latency spike
operator play: If region enters AGGRESSIVE_DEGRADE - notify infra, run rollback-degrade.sh, escalate to on-call lead if pages persist > 15m

comments:
2026-03-01 - Evelyn Park: Initial ticket created after postmortem for intermittent capacity storms. Goal: reduce noisy pages and give on-call safe mitigation steps.
2026-03-03 - Rajat Singh: Spike completed. SLO heat scoring function using 5m/1h windows looks promising; will prototype SLIGHT_DEGRADE that reduces embedding batch size and disables analytics route.
2026-03-05 - UX Review (private): Need clear operator UI for 'why did this degrade' with links to recent deploys and infra events. Assigned to PM to scope Console card.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1189 - circuit-breaker state machine + mocks. Asking for review from @marie and @cheng.
2026-03-09 - Integration test note: Synthetic storm in staging shows automatic SLIGHT_DEGRADE prevented a region-wide latency spike but AGGRESSIVE_DEGRADE caused error increase for noncritical routes. Tuning required.
2026-03-10 - Rajat Singh: Adjusted threshold to use adaptive percentile (p90->p95 shift) and added hysteresis window to avoid flapping. Preparing runbook scriptlets for reviewer feedback.
